caption: Kar. 98. Altar
reading: wo si : so(2)reyi : ns(3)yedḫeto qo wi : ntki(4)li tedḫl?owi : aeq?ykr : (5)terikel?owi : ato mẖ : pso(6)ẖte : at (7)mẖ : psḫ(8)rkete : (9)ḫmlol : p(10)ẖ?olkete : pqr(11)leb : yetmdelowi : peseto(12)leb : kdito wi : mlo (13)mrse n(14)lotete(15)lowi :
notes: Copy line 1: the y after ns is four strokes, the first long and dipping below the line. d here and in tedḫ is the hooked-lambda form (could be ñ). 'qo' = slash + closed 3 (q) then a slash (o); the same group ends the first clause in Kar. 99, 101 and 102. Line 2: tedḫ?owi has only one small sign between ḫ and o (read l; e+l expected). Line 3: se? could be b + o; the l of terikelowi is drawn dotted. Line 4: 'ms' is a tailed 3 then a plain 3 in both benedictions; 'so' in pso(6)ẖte could be q. Line 6: q? is slash + closed 3. Line 8: first sign tailed 3 (m or ẖ); n? is a bare 2 with a long tail; 'l?o' before (15) is an unbarred zigzag sign; barred /ϟ read te, unbarred read lo. Throughout: tailed 3 read m, plain 3 read s; Σ-topped long-tailed sign read k, ξ-topped read p.
check_notes: All 27 entries placed. The names table confirms ns(3)yedḫetoqowi and ntki(4)li as read; the type changed the father's name, the benediction words mẖ (twice), and the descriptions (p for my k, m for my 3-shapes, e for my l?). tedḫl?owi has no entry and stays.

caption: Kar. 99. Altar
reading: wo si : sor(2)eyi : mke[.][.](3)[.][.]li qo w?i : y?ilmen(4)k : ter?ikel?owi : de[.][.]kye (5)tedḫelowi : ato m(6)ẖe : psoẖeb(7)ẖte : (8)ḫmlol : yi(9)doteni ye(10)bḫtei? : mo dyeye(11)qo wi : nkeli : terike(12)lowi : mkedeqoli (13)tedḫelow?i (14)ato mẖe : (15)psoẖekte : ḫ(16)mlol?i? : ḫlm?w?i? : pi(17)sikl?e?kte : (18)mlo rtebk?wi :
notes: Line 1: after k a heavily inked (damaged) sign read d?; hatching of about four signs with (3) in it; w of the final wi is hatched. Line 2: the opening 'yii' is a tangle of 4-forms and strokes; r? in terikelowi is a flat V, not the usual ω. Line 3: e? is hatched; hatching of about two signs. Line 4: ñ? is a crossed sign with a loop; b is an angle form. Line 5: two barred te-like signs, the second ligatured with a 4 (te? i); the last two signs are hatched. Line 6 has no divider at its end. Line 7 and 9: n? is a bare 2 with a long flat tail (n or a); t? in line 9 is a blob-headed hook. Line 10: 'sic' stands over the hatched w in ḫlmw?y; the order there (ḫ l m) differs from the ḫmlol of other texts. Line 11: Griffith prints a small ? over the b; the first three signs are S-forms (l e e).
check_notes: All 29 entries placed. Two persons: person 1 in copy lines 1-3, person 2 in lines 6-8. Formula A has parts a (line 4) and b (line 9), formula C part a is line 5, formula H part b is line 10. The type made my tailed 3 = ẖ and plain 3 = m in mẖe. Line 9: Griffith calls the first word a bad writing of ato resembling ab; I take ato. Line 11 (mlo mrtebkwi): the copy shows no second m.

caption: Kar. 100. Altar
reading: wo si : sore(2)yi : pedemoketme(3)qewi : pqrl : yetemde lo si : (4)pestol : se wilowi : (5)at mḫe : pi(6)siḫr(7)kte : a(8)to mẖo : pisi(9)ẖte : ḫmlo(10)l : yidote ni(11)kte :
notes: Line 1: the k after kede has a 3-like head and long tail (k or ẖ); 'sl?' is a small S then 3; (3) stands over a tailed 3 with a single slash after it (m o, or q). Line 2: 'si' (4 crossed with 3) carries 'sic'; 'sewi lowi' follows the copy literally. Line 3: the a before (8)to is hatched and marked 'sic'. Line 4: ñ? is the hooked lambda form (ñ or d).
check_notes: All 20 entries placed. The name (names table pedemoketmeqewi) takes 15 of my 16 copy signs with my slash+3 as q. lo si (marked sic in the copy) is kept against the type's lowi.

caption: Kar. 101. Altar
reading: wo si : a(2)soreyi : ten?[.](3)dḫito qo wi : mlosḫi(4)li : yerikelowi : metemnise(5)li : tedḫelowi : [.][.][.][.]r?(6)p?ḫli : sem lo(7)wi : pese(8)toli : sem lo (9)lowi : ssorli (10)kdiselowi : ḫm(11)loli : ẖ?lkte ato mẖe pi(12)siẖte : at mẖe (13)yiḫrkte (14)dbotelito (15)qo wi : mlolowi : yeto(16)str : yerikelowi : (17)kdey?e?t : tedḫ?elowi : ḫm(18)loli : ẖ[.]lkte : (19)ḫmloli : iplte :
notes: Line 1: 'asoreyi' (an a before soreyi) as copied; one hatched sign before (3). Lines 2 and 8: 'yerikelowi' has three strokes (y) where te is expected; I follow the copy. Line 4: the start is a dotted stretch of about four signs, then hatched i? and d?; 'sic' stands over the first /ϟ of 'ses lo (9)lowi'. Lines 5 and 9: the 4+ϟ ligature in ḫmlol read as one l. Line 6: the a is partly hatched; in the second half two hatched signs (m? l?) before (13). Line 7: ñ? is a looped crossed sign. Line 9: Griffith prints a ? over a hatched sign, given as [.]. In each copy line the right half is read before the left half, as the line numbers run.
check_notes: All 46 entries placed. Two persons: person 1 in copy lines 1-3, person 2 in lines 7-8. Formula C parts a, b, c are line 5 left, line 9 right and line 9 left. The 4+ϟ ligature is l + i (ḫmloli), as the type shows. yerikelowi (with y) is confirmed by Index C. The opening of line 4 is dotted in the copy; the type reads ḫr[p]ḫli there.

caption: Kar. 102. Stela, on Pl. 27.
notes: Stela with cracks drawn as wavy lines; signs drawn in thin outline (doubtful traces) are marked ?. Copy line 1: the first sign is a bold S-form crossed by a crack (s or e). Copy line 2: 'nii?' is a long-tailed n followed by two crossed 4-forms. Copy line 4: it opens (at the right) with a w i group, then thin l?o?; the dotted stretches are counted dot by dot (10 and 15). Copy line 5: a? is S2 crossed by crack lines, preceded (to its left) by a bold angle read ḫ?; the dots before (7) may include a divider. Copy lines 5-6: ʒ with a long tail under ν read k and ν read b, giving -lebkwi.
check_notes: 15 of 17 entries placed; 'mẖo' (form A) and the empty names-table row for person 1 ('lost') are not found. Person 2: bk[.][.][.][.]qowi and wilo... confirmed. The copy has one more crossed 4 between soni and mnitowi; it is kept as i?.
